ONGOING STORY — Updated 16 July 2026 at 19:13. 16 source updates have been combined into this article.

Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood has outlined plans to deport Shabir Ahmed, the leader of the Rochdale grooming gang, following his release from prison after serving 14 years for multiple sexual offences.

Latest update

The UK government is considering implementing visa restrictions in response to Pakistan's refusal to accept responsibility for Shabir Ahmed, a convicted rapist associated with Rochdale.

Ahmed, who was sentenced to 19 years in prison for his crimes, has been a focal point in discussions regarding international accountability for serious offences.

The potential visa restrictions aim to address concerns over the lack of cooperation from Pakistan in dealing with Ahmed's case and similar issues.

This development highlights ongoing tensions between the UK and Pakistan regarding the handling of criminal matters involving British nationals.

Earlier developments

Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood has announced plans to facilitate the deportation of Shabir Ahmed, the leader of the Rochdale grooming gang, after his release from prison. Ahmed, who was convicted in 2012 for multiple counts of rape and sexual offences against girls, was released on 2 July after serving 14 years of a 22-year sentence.

The government is considering visa restrictions on Pakistan if it does not accept Ahmed back. Mahmood stated that she intends to amend the Immigration and Asylum Bill to remove legal barriers preventing his deportation under the 1971 Immigration Act. However, she acknowledged that deportation is contingent upon Pakistan's agreement to take him back.

In response, Pakistan's Foreign Office has rejected the notion of accepting Ahmed, asserting that the responsibility for his crimes lies with the UK, where he was raised and groomed. This statement marks the first time Pakistan has publicly refused to take back the convicted offender. Tahir Andrabi, a spokesman for the Foreign Office, stated that the onus lies with the UK for allowing Ahmed to commit his crimes.

The situation has sparked significant public outcry, particularly regarding Ahmed's initial placement in Accrington, where he was housed near a playground and a mosque. Following concerns raised by local officials and the community, he has since been relocated outside the borough.

Update timeline

  • 19:13 BST, 16 July 2026: UK Considers Visa Restrictions Following Pakistan's Rejection of Responsibility for Shabir Ahmed
  • 01:01 BST, 14 July 2026: Rochdale Ringleader’s Deportation Not Linked to Pakistan
